chohealth.name: CHOHEALTH
chohealth.tagline: Healthcare booking, self-hosted end to end
chohealth.description: An end-to-end telemedicine platform: appointment scheduling, online payments, medical consultations, prescriptions, lab orders, invoicing and pharmacy delivery — built and deployed entirely on my own infrastructure.
chohealth.problem: Small clinics were juggling paper schedules and disconnected tools for booking, billing and records — nothing talked to each other, and double-bookings were routine.
chohealth.stats: 25+ database models · 70+ REST endpoints · 40+ frontend routes
features: A scheduling engine that validates working hours, breaks, service duration and appointment conflicts before a slot is confirmed
Three-layer booking protection: frontend validation, DRF serializer validation, and database constraints
Stripe and PayPal payments with idempotent webhook handling and audited refund workflows
Atomic consultation flow — diagnosis, prescriptions and lab orders are created together or not at all
Invoices, prescriptions and lab orders generated as real PDF documents with ReportLab
QR pickup codes, SendGrid transactional email, and full English/Spanish support

decisions.title: Booking conflicts are prevented at the database layer, not just in view logic
decisions.rationale: A conditional unique constraint on (doctor, date) is the last line of defense against a race condition where two patients pay for the same slot within milliseconds of each other. App-level checks give a fast, friendly error; the constraint is what actually guarantees correctness under concurrency.

decisions.title: A polymorphic Invoice via two nullable one-to-one fields plus a CheckConstraint, instead of a generic foreign key
decisions.rationale: Keeps referential integrity and normal SQL joins on Invoice.appointment / Invoice.medicine_order, while a database-level XOR check makes it structurally impossible to bill both — or neither — from the same invoice, even if a future view has a bug.

decisions.title: Role is stored on the user, but never trusted alone for authorization
decisions.rationale: Custom permissions check the role and that the related profile object actually exists. A user who claims a role without a matching profile is not authorized — closing a gap a naive role check would leave open.

decisions.title: Denormalized doctor rating, kept in sync via signals
decisions.rationale: The doctor list/search is a hot read path; recomputing an average on every request doesn't scale as reviews grow, so a post_save/post_delete signal on Review recalculates and persists the aggregate instead.

decisions.title: One shared Stripe webhook for both appointments and pharmacy orders, routed by metadata
decisions.rationale: Avoids duplicating signature verification and event handling for two billable entity types — the invoice/payment model already treats them polymorphically, so the webhook mirrors that.

limitations: Delivery tracking is simulated, not real — there's no courier integration or webhook. Each order's stage is computed from elapsed time since payment, not from a real-world event.
A doctor's weekly availability can currently only be created or edited through the Django admin — there's no self-service "manage my availability" endpoint yet.

choplanner.name: CHO Planner
choplanner.description: A personal task and note manager in the spirit of Linear or ClickUp, deliberately simpler — with a swappable AI assistant that breaks goals into weighted subtasks and an optional Google Calendar sync.
choplanner.problem: Most task managers either lock you into their cloud or hand your data — and your AI provider's API key — to a third party. I wanted something I fully own: self-hosted, with AI as an optional layer, not a dependency.
features: Swappable AI assistant — bring your own Claude, GPT or Gemini key; every provider's output is validated against the same Zod schema before it touches the database
Kanban board with drag-and-drop, weighted task priorities, sprints and Markdown notes
Optional Google Calendar sync via OAuth 2.0, always with explicit confirmation before writing an event
API keys and refresh tokens encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM — never sent back to the frontend
Installable PWA with an offline page and a service worker that never caches API routes

neurostock.name: Neurostock
neurostock.tagline: Stock price prediction with LSTM neural networks
neurostock.description: Predicts stock prices for any ticker using an LSTM neural network trained on historical data from Yahoo Finance, with backtesting and confidence intervals — not just a single-number guess.
features: 2-layer LSTM (128 + 64 units) trained on up to 10 years of historical price data per ticker
Monte Carlo Dropout (50 iterations) to turn a single prediction into a real confidence interval
Strict separation between train and test scalers to prevent data leakage — a mistake most tutorials skip
Backtesting dashboard with MSE, RMSE and R² computed against real historical prices
JWT auth with automatic token refresh, and a singleton-cached model for fast concurrent predictions

sevenlever.name: Seven Lever
sevenlever.description: A local two-player dice game based on "Seven Eleven", the game played in Colombian schoolyards — bets, a life bar, and an animated loss sequence, all live in the frontend.
features: The full ruleset: target-number logic, instant loss on 7 or 11, a configurable life bar (3–10 hits)
Game logic runs 100% in the frontend for zero-latency turns — the backend only persists finished rounds
Framer Motion animations for the dice roll, the "seal" hit, and the crying loss sequence
Local two-player state in Zustand; match history and stats persisted through Prisma
Sound effects via Howler.js, lazy-loaded so they never block first paint
